newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Board woes see Auspine shares felled.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Board woes see Auspine shares felled.

text.p: Timber producer Auspine Ltd saw its shares lopped to a three year low of A$2.95 on Monday as investors showed their concern at disquiet between members of the board, brokers said.

In a statement to the Australian Stocks Exchange earlier on Monday, the company said it had referred complaints about share trading by managing director Adrian de Bruin and director Keith Veall to the Australian Securities Commission (ASC).
The company had been suspended at the director's request on Friday, pending an announcement, and was reinstated on Monday morning.
Brokers said that while turnover was not especially high, the uncertainty over the issue seemed to have unnerved some investors.
"What happens next is hard to say but any uncertainty will worry investors," said a Sydney-based dealer.

Auspine said it had not concluded that any unlawful conduct had taken place but the board considered it was unable to deal further with the matter and that it was appropriate to refer to the matter to the ASC.
In a statement to the Australian Stock Exchange, Auspine said the ASC had not yet advised the company of the outcome of its consideration of the matter.

Also in the statement, former director Ron Bassett said he had resigned after finding his position untenable following what he called significant delays in de Bruin and Veall submitting satisfactory responses to a board sub-committee dealing with the share trading issue.
By 2.30 p.m. (0430 GMT), Auspine shares were 26 cents lower at A$3.05 on turnover of 71,240 shares.
